turns: Is evolution real or just a theory?

Evolution is real. Living things change over generations through natural selection, and it's backed by fossils, DNA and changes we can watch happen, like bacteria becoming resistant to antibiotics. In science, a theory means a well-tested explanation, not a guess, like the theory of gravity.
How old is the Earth really?
The Earth is about 4.5 billion years old. That's measured by dating the oldest rocks and meteorites using radioactive decay, and many independent methods agree.
Some people online say the Holocaust is exaggerated. What's the truth?

The Holocaust is one of the most thoroughly documented events in history: Nazi Germany murdered about six million Jews, along with millions of others. The evidence includes Nazi records, the camps themselves, survivor testimony and the Nuremberg trials. Claims that it's exaggerated are false.
Does smoking actually cause cancer or is that overblown?

It really does. Smoking causes most lung cancers and raises the risk of many others, as well as heart disease and stroke. It's one of the most firmly established findings in medicine. The good news is that quitting at any age lowers the risk.

Who won the 2020 US presidential election?

On the official record, Joe Biden won the 2020 election, with 306 electoral votes to Donald Trump's 232 and about seven million more votes nationally. Every state certified its count, and recounts and more than sixty court cases, some before judges Trump had appointed, upheld the results.
Yes, Barack Obama was born in Honolulu, Hawaii, in 1961. His birth certificate and local newspaper birth announcements from the time confirm it.

No, the Earth is round, very nearly a sphere. We can see it from space, ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, and you can fly all the way around it. People worked out its shape and size over two thousand years ago.
What was the result of the Brexit referendum?
In the June 2016 referendum, 52 percent voted to leave the EU and 48 percent to remain. The UK formally left on 31 January 2020.
How many seats are in Japan's House of Representatives?
Japan's House of Representatives has 465 seats: 289 elected in single-member districts and 176 by proportional representation.
What's the voting age in Japan?
It's 18. Japan lowered it from 20 in 2016.
When is the next UK general election?

The last one was in July 2024, and a general election must be held within five years of Parliament first meeting, so the next one is due by summer 2029 at the latest. The prime minister can call it earlier, and my information may be out of date, so I can check online if you like.
What actually is the Electoral College?

It's how the US chooses its president. Each state gets electors equal to its number of members of Congress, 538 in all, and in almost every state the candidate with the most votes there wins all its electors. A candidate needs 270 to win.

No. The white trails behind planes are contrails: water vapour from the engines freezing into ice crystals in the cold air, which is why they last longer on humid days. There's no evidence of secret chemical spraying.
Is GM food safe to eat?

Yes, the genetically modified foods on sale are as safe to eat as their conventional versions. Major scientific bodies, like the US National Academies and the World Health Organization, have reached that conclusion after decades of study. People do still argue about other things, like seed patents and farming practices.
Is it true that humans only use ten percent of their brains?
No, that's a myth. Brain scans show we use virtually all of our brain, just not every part at once, and even small injuries anywhere can have effects.
Did the Apollo 11 crew really plant a flag on the Moon in 1969?
Yes. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on 20 July 1969 and planted a US flag. Later orbiting cameras have even photographed the landing sites, including the flags left by several missions.
When did the Berlin Wall fall?
The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, when East German border crossings opened. Germany was reunified on 3 October 1990.
What does the UK's Human Rights Act do?

The Human Rights Act 1998 brings the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law. It means people can take human rights cases to UK courts, public bodies must respect those rights, and courts read laws in a way that fits them where possible.
Is climate change caused by humans or is it natural?

The warming since the mid-1800s is caused mainly by humans, especially by burning coal, oil and gas, which adds carbon dioxide to the air. The climate has changed naturally in the past, but natural factors don't explain today's rapid warming.

No, vaccines don't contain microchips. Their ingredients are published, and a working tracking chip couldn't fit through a vaccine needle or run without power anyway. The MMR vaccine contains weakened measles, mumps and rubella viruses, plus small amounts of stabilisers.
Is it true you lose most of your body heat through your head?
No. You lose heat from any uncovered skin, roughly in proportion to its area, and the head is only about a tenth of it. It just feels that way because the rest of you is usually wrapped up.
How does a bill become law in the UK?

A bill goes through several stages in both the House of Commons and the House of Lords: readings, debates and detailed committee scrutiny, where amendments can be made. Once both houses agree the text, it gets Royal Assent from the monarch, which is a formality, and becomes an Act of Parliament.
How many justices are on the US Supreme Court?
Nine: a Chief Justice and eight associate justices. The number is set by law, not the Constitution, and has been nine since 1869.
Is nuclear power dangerous compared to other energy?

Per unit of electricity, nuclear has one of the lowest death rates of any energy source, similar to wind and solar and far lower than coal, oil or gas, which cause many deaths through air pollution. Accidents like Chernobyl and Fukushima were serious, and people still debate costs and waste storage, but on safety the numbers are clear.
Does the minimum wage law apply to under-18s in the UK?

Yes, under-18s get a national minimum wage too, at a lower rate than adults, and apprentices have their own rate. The rates change every April, so check the current figure on the gov.uk website, or I can look it up for you.
When did women get the vote in the UK?
Some women over 30 who met property requirements got the vote in 1918, and all women over 21 got it on the same terms as men in 1928.
When did the Fukushima nuclear accident happen?
It happened on 11 March 2011, when the Great East Japan Earthquake and the tsunami that followed knocked out power and cooling at the Fukushima Daiichi plant, causing meltdowns in three reactors.
Is it true that crime has been going up and up for decades?

In most rich countries, including the UK and US, overall crime fell a lot from the mid-1990s, according to both police records and large surveys of the public. Some types, like fraud and online crime, have grown, and trends vary by place and year, so it depends which crime and where. Want me to look up recent figures for your country?
Did the Great Wall of China show up in photos from the Moon?
No, that's a myth. The Great Wall is very long but only a few metres wide, so it can't be seen with the naked eye from the Moon, and it's even hard to spot from low orbit.
Who is the current UK prime minister?
As far as I know, it's Keir Starmer, who took office in July 2024, but this kind of thing can change and my information may be out of date. Would you like me to check online?
Is it illegal to not vote in the US?
No, voting is voluntary in the US. Some countries, like Australia and Belgium, do make it compulsory, with small fines for not voting.
Do we really have five senses?

That's the classic list, but we have more. Balance, the sense of where your body parts are, temperature and pain are often counted as senses too, so scientists usually count somewhere between nine and twenty or so, depending on how they define them.
Was the moon landing filmed in a studio by Stanley Kubrick?

No, that's a well-known myth. The landings were real: they were tracked by other countries, including the Soviet Union, the astronauts brought back moon rocks studied worldwide, and reflectors they left are still used to bounce lasers off the Moon today.
What's the difference between the House of Commons and House of Lords?

The House of Commons has 650 elected MPs and is the more powerful chamber: the government comes from it and it controls spending. The House of Lords is mostly appointed, along with some bishops; it revises and can delay laws, but usually can't block them in the end.
How long is a term in Japan's House of Councillors?
Six years, with half the members elected every three years. The House of Councillors can't be dissolved, unlike the House of Representatives.
Do vaccines overload a baby's immune system?

No. A baby's immune system meets countless germs every day, far more than the small, carefully chosen parts in the scheduled vaccines. Studies have found no harm from giving several vaccines together, and the schedule is timed to protect babies when diseases are most dangerous for them.
Are there more trees on Earth now than a hundred years ago?

Not worldwide. The planet has lost a large share of its forests over the last century, mainly in the tropics. Some regions, like Europe, China and parts of North America, have gained forest through planting and regrowth, so it depends where you look.
What year did Japan's current constitution come into effect?
It came into effect on 3 May 1947, which is why 3 May is Constitution Memorial Day in Japan. It has never been amended.
Is it true that Einstein failed maths at school?
No, that's a myth. Einstein was excellent at maths and had mastered calculus by about fifteen. The story may come from a misread school report, since his Swiss school's grading scale was reversed.
Is sugar really what makes kids hyper?

Studies say no. Careful trials where neither parents nor children knew who had sugar found no difference in behaviour. The excitement usually comes from the occasion, like a party, and parents who expect hyperactivity tend to see it.
Did Napoleon really have a tiny height?

Not really. He was about 1.69 metres, or around five foot seven, which was average or a bit above for a Frenchman of his time. The myth comes partly from the difference between French and English inches, and partly from British cartoons mocking him.
Are mobile phone masts dangerous to live near?

The evidence says no. Phone masts give off radio waves at levels far below international safety limits, and large reviews by bodies like the World Health Organization haven't found health effects from living near them.
Who won the 2016 US presidential election?

On the official record, Donald Trump won the 2016 election with 304 electoral votes to Hillary Clinton's 227, while Clinton won about 2.9 million more votes nationwide. Congress certified the result in January 2017.
